adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Nigeria
adds.summary: Nigeria's federal framework, which governs Plateau, criminalises same-sex sexual activity: punishable by death in the 12 northern states with Shari'a law and by up to 14 years' imprisonment in the southern portion and under northern secular law, with the Same Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2013 extending criminalisation to attempted same-sex marriages. It reports no legal protections for LGBTQ+ people and frequent violence against them, and it records a 2022 legal challenge in which a court ruled Sections 4(1), 5(2) and 5(3) of the 2013 Act unconstitutional and unenforceable in any part of the country.

adds.title: Plateau State (Wikipedia)
adds.summary: Confirms Plateau is a Nigerian state in the North Central geopolitical zone, with its capital at Jos and a population of around 4.7 million. This places the jurisdiction in the north-central zone the record's existing source describes as bearing the national climate of arrests and communal tension most heavily, with no Shari'a-criminal-law status claimed for the state.

adds.title: Anambra State (Wikipedia)
adds.summary: Confirms Anambra is a Nigerian state in the Southeastern region, Igbo-majority, formed in 1976, with capital Awka. Its southeastern (southern) location places it outside the northern zone where the sources' Shari'a-criminal-law states sit, so the federal penalties apply in full while the northern Sharia provisions do not reach this state, matching the record's positioning.
